title: Nimbus Pay - POC scoping: workload modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for a conversational payments assistant and fraud triage. Agreed success criteria: p95 latency <450ms for interactive flows, end-to-end accuracy parity within 3% vs current baseline, cost target <$0.0025 per request. Needed artifacts: sample traces, token distributions, SAML/SOC2 docs. Next step: Redwood to run a 1-hour benchmark and share results; customer to provide 24h sample workload and SSO contact.
next_steps: Redwood: run 1-hour throughput test at target QPS and share results (by 2027-07-26)
Nimbus: provide 24h sample request traces and token histograms (by 2027-07-23)
Schedule canary run on Dedicated if benchmarks meet SLOs (tentative week of 2027-08-02)
action_items: Priya (SE): run 1-hour throughput test with 2k requests, step QPS 10->80, capture p50/p95/p99 and token breakdown - due 2027-07-26
Samira (CTO): share 24h request logs and a few example prompts/redactions - due 2027-07-23
Jordan (AE): send pricing sheet and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff doc - due 2027-07-22
transcript:
00:00 Jordan: ok good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. we have priya from our se team. could you introduce quickly? 00:08 Samira: hi all, samira here, cto at nimbus, we run payments rails and want to scope a poc for a conversational payments assistant plus a fraud triage model. 00:16 Jordan: great, objective today — workload characterization and traffic modeling; want to make sure POC success criteria are measurable. 00:22 Ethan: yep, we want to validate latency and cost at our peak qps and confirm model quality. quick context, prod has about 200k MAUs, about 15k active daily users, our chat flow is triggered roughly 0.5x per active user per day, so ~7.5k requests/day baseline, peak burst patterns during batch settlements. 00:40 Rafael: from infra side, our bursts can hit short spikes where concurrency jumps x10 for 1-3 minutes, so we care about graceful degradation. 00:50 Priya: thanks, that's useful. can you walk us through request shape? input length, expected outputs, and any system messages? 00:57 Ethan: typical user prompt is 30-70 tokens, median around 48. reply length med is 110 tokens, but for receipts or dispute details can go to 400 tokens occasionally. 01:10 Samira: also some calls are embeddings for search, small 32-token inputs, and we have reranking flows that send 5 candidates for a single query. 01:20 Priya: ok so we should model a mix: 70% interactive chat (48 in / 110 out), 20% long-form (80 in / 250 out), 10% embedding/rerank small inputs. 01:32 Jordan: what's your p95 latency SLO target for the interactive flow? 01:36 Samira: we want p95 < 450ms ideally; p99 under 900ms. anything above that and product team balks. 01:44 Priya: understood. for cost targets — do you have a per-request budget or TCO target? 01:49 Ethan: we are aiming for <$0.0025 per request averaged across the mix, because we do math against payment margins. 01:57 Rafael: and from security we require SOC2 and SAML SSO, and for private data residency we need to confirm keys with KMS, maybe dedicated or private deployment. 02:07 Priya: ok noted. for the POC we typically run on hosted but can spin up a small Dedicated capacity to validate throughput; Dedicated gives predictable throughput at cost but takes a few days to reserve. 02:18 Jordan: quick Q — what's your expected QPS distribution across the day? 02:22 Samira: baseline QPS averaged at 0.08 (7.5k/day -> ~0.087), peak sustained windows reach 40-60 QPS for 3-5 minutes during settlement, and rare extreme bursts up to 120 QPS for <1 minute. 02:40 Priya: got it. to size GPU pools we care about sustained QPS and average concurrency. what's your average concurrency target? 02:46 Ethan: during peak windows we measure concurrency ~45-55 concurrent requests; typical concurrency mid-day ~10-15. 02:54 Priya: ok, for modeling i'll assume concurrency 50 at peak, 15 baseline. batching and kv cache can reduce effective token compute for repeated prefixes. do you have many repeated prefixes? 03:05 Samira: yes, about 30% of requests are similar prompts (status checks), so prefix caching could help. 03:12 Priya: great, that reduces per-token cost. another factor is kv cache hit vs miss rates for multi-turn chat — do you expect long sessions? 03:20 Ethan: most sessions are short, 1-3 turns; kv miss rate roughly 60%. 03:25 Priya: noted. i'll model with 40% cache hit. 03:29 Jordan: let's translate that into model throughput. for a common 48in/110out example, that's ~158 tokens total per request. at 50 concurrent requests, that's 7.9k tokens in flight; with Redwood runtime and batching we can push high throughput but latency SLO is tight. 03:46 Priya: operationally, for POC we'll run two benchmark passes: 1) tail-latency pass with steady concurrency at target 50 concurrent, measuring p50/p95/p99 and packet drop; 2) throughput pass with step-up QPS from 10 -> 80 to find knee. 04:01 Samira: sounds good. what hardware are you planning to use in the benchmark? 04:05 Priya: for the hosted benchmark we'll use ampere A100-ish or similar instance type depending on the model size; if you want Dedicated we can reserve an 8-GPU pool to emulate production. 04:16 Ethan: we need cost estimates for hosted inference vs a small dedicated pool. 04:20 Jordan: i'll include that in the pricing sheet, but high level — hosted is faster to run, dedicated gives lower unit costs at sustained load. 04:28 Rafael: also, we need model quantization considerations; we are okay with int8 if it preserves perf. 04:33 Priya: we do recommend quantized variants for cost savings; we'll run quality regressions on your eval set to confirm within 3% accuracy delta. 04:41 Samira: can you run the benchmark against our eval set? we have a labeled fraud triage dataset of ~5k prompts. 04:48 Priya: yes please send that as redacted CSV, we'll run a quality pass and regressions during the POC. 04:55 Jordan: let's capture success criteria so everyone is aligned — i've got some notes: 1) p95 < 450ms on interactive mix, 2) quality delta vs baseline < 3% F1 on triage dataset, 3) cost < $0.0025 per request averaged. any changes? 05:13 Ethan: add availability target for the POC — 99.5% uptime across test windows. 05:18 Jordan: added. 05:20 Rafael: for security review, you'll need to provide SOC2 docs and an SSO contact; we'll do a brief security sign-off before any dedicated provisioning. 05:28 Priya: we can share SOC2 and our security pack; send over an SSO test account if you want to validate SAML. 05:34 Samira: timeline? how long from benchmark to dedicated can we expect? 05:38 Jordan: benchmark results shared within 2 business days after the run; if metrics look good, Dedicated reservation typically takes 3-5 business days to provision for a small pool. so optimistic path is 2 weeks to a canary. 05:50 Priya: operational details for the benchmark: please provide a 24-hour sample of traces with timestamps, distribution of tokens per request, and percent of multi-turn sessions. that'll let us synthesize a realistic traffic profile and ensure step-up tests match reality. 06:03 Samira: we'll redact PII and send. 06:07 Ethan: a few nitty-gritty items: do you support auto-batching and prefix caching out of the box; can we tune batch size / latency tradeoff? 06:15 Priya: yes, runtime supports continuous batching and has knobs for max batch size and latency cap; we also have prefix/KV cache features and quantization profiles we can toggle. 06:25 Rafael: what observability will we get during the POC? traces, token-level cost, per-model dashboards? 06:31 Jordan: Redwood Console will show per-route token breakdown, p95 latency, and cost estimates; we'll provide a shared dashboard for the POC. 06:39 Priya: one more question on reranking flows — you said you send 5 candidates, do you rerank with a single model call or use embeddings + MMR? 06:47 Ethan: currently embeddings for candidate retrieval then lightweight re-rank; some calls re-rank client-side so POC should model both. 06:54 Priya: ok i'll include a 5% heavy rerank path in the synthetic profile. 06:58 Jordan: to make sure the next steps are actionable: priya will run the benchmark once we get sample traces; jordan will send pricing and security docs; nimbus provides redacted logs and labeled eval set. 07:09 Samira: agreed. also please include a note about fallback strategy if capacity constrained — we need graceful degradation not 500s. 07:17 Priya: we have model variant fallback and region failover; we'll test that as part of the canary. 07:22 Rafael: final: can you include the exact benchmark script so our infra team can peer review? 07:26 Priya: yes, we'll include the script and a k6/locust profile. 07:30 Jordan: wrap up — i'll email summary and next steps. thanks everyone. 07:34 Samira: thanks, bye. 07:36 (meeting ends)

Note: transcript contains occasional misheard tokens and name variants; references to KV cache appear as k v cache in some parts.
